pr.title: Send a practice's report link to its HubSpot contact, behind a marketing flag

decisions.title: Marketing is a pure passthrough — forward three fields, touch no storage
decisions.rejected: Have marketing read S3 / call Couchdrop / hold Couchdrop credentials to build the link itself
decisions.why: Scoping the marketing side to a passthrough keeps the blast radius tiny: it reads no S3, calls no Couchdrop, and holds no Couchdrop credentials. Every field it sends arrives on the event; the payload builder is the whole of its data handling. That is what lets this ship as a small, low-impact change.
decisions.quote: Marketing is a pure passthrough — it forwards couchdrop_shared_link_url + practice_email + email_type straight through; it reads no S3, calls no Couchdrop, and holds no Couchdrop credentials.

evidence.claim: The entire payload is three fields lifted off the message — no fetch, no credential, no enrichment.

decisions.title: Gate the send behind a flag that ships off, keyed on practice with no PHI
decisions.chose: Evaluate marketing-practice-report-send-enabled with context { kind: "practice", key: practice_sf_account_id }, fallback false.
decisions.rejected: Ship the send path live, or key the flag on the recipient / patient
decisions.why: The flag ships off and is flipped on deliberately after deploy, so the new path changes no behaviour until intended — and flipping it off withholds sends during a HubSpot incident with no redeploy. The context carries only the Salesforce account id, never a recipient or patient identifier, so no PHI/PII reaches LaunchDarkly. It fails closed: an unreachable flag source withholds rather than sends.
decisions.quote: Context is { kind: "practice", key: practice_sf_account_id } (no PHI/PII in context). Fails closed (fallback: false); an unreachable flag source withholds.

evidence.claim: The flag key, the practice-only context, and the false fallback are all set at the one call site.

decisions.title: Give the practice-report send its own payload type — don't widen the union
decisions.chose: Add HubSpotPracticeReportWebhookPayload as a separate type, accepted by sendHubSpotWebhook via a union at the parameter.
decisions.rejected: Add the practice-report case as a member of the existing HubSpotWebhookPayload union
decisions.why: The partner-referral HubSpotWebhookPayload union is closed over its EmailType, and buildPartnerReferralWebhookPayload relies on that closure to narrow. Adding a practice-report member would break that narrowing. A separate type carries no per-patient enrichment fields and leaves the existing union — and every consumer that narrows on it — untouched.
decisions.quote: Deliberately not a member of HubSpotWebhookPayload: that union is closed over the partner-referral EmailType, and widening it breaks narrowing in buildPartnerReferralWebhookPayload.

evidence.claim: The new type stands alone; sendHubSpotWebhook accepts it as an added arm of a parameter union, so the closed partner-referral union is never widened.

decisions.title: Decompose the handler into gate → claim → send
decisions.chose: Split practiceReportGenerated into three guard-clause steps: is-send-enabled, claim-slot, send-claimed.
decisions.rejected: One method that flag-checks, claims, composes, POSTs, and releases inline
decisions.why: Each step is a guard that returns early, so the happy path reads top to bottom and each precondition is checkable in isolation. It mirrors the established PartnerReferralSubscription flow (flag → claim → send → release-on-failure), so a reviewer who knows that precedent already knows this shape.

decisions.title: Claim an idempotency slot so redelivery never double-sends
decisions.chose: Claim (practice_id, report_type, batch_period) before sending; a lost claim refuses the send.
decisions.rejected: Send on every delivery, or check-then-insert (racy under concurrent partitions)
decisions.why: Kafka is at-least-once and the consumer runs four partitions concurrently, so the same report can arrive more than once. The claim is an atomic INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING on a unique key; a redelivery loses the claim and makes no HubSpot request. That turns duplicate delivery into a no-op instead of a duplicate email.
decisions.quote: claim uses INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (practice_id, report_type, batch_period) DO NOTHING; redelivery under at-least-once semantics refuses the claim and makes no HubSpot request.

decisions.title: Release the slot on send failure so a later flip re-drives cleanly
decisions.chose: Track a sent flag; in finally, release the claim if the send did not succeed, then rethrow.
decisions.rejected: Leave the slot claimed on failure (permanent), or release unconditionally
decisions.why: A claimed-but-unsent slot would permanently block that report — a HubSpot outage would silently swallow it forever. Releasing only on failure means a retry, or a later flag flip, re-drives cleanly; releasing unconditionally would defeat the idempotency guard on the success path. Rethrowing preserves the consumer's at-least-once retry semantics.
decisions.quote: a later flip re-drives cleanly since flag-off never claims a slot.
